William hides Easter candy in the cabinet above the refrigerator. His wife then moves the candy from that cabinet to the pantry while William helps her organize the kitchen. Where will William look for the Easter candy?

Grace puts her painting brushes in the ceramic jar on her art table and goes to wash her hands. While Grace is washing her hands, her mother moves the brushes from the ceramic jar to a wooden case on the shelf. Grace returns to the art table. Where will Grace look for her painting brushes?

Amelia leaves her phone on the coffee table and walks to the mailbox. While Amelia is at the mailbox, her brother picks up the phone and plugs it in to charge on the kitchen counter. Amelia comes back from the mailbox. Where will Amelia look for her phone?

Anthony leaves his medication on the nightstand and goes to brush his teeth. While Anthony is in the bathroom, his wife moves the medication from the nightstand to the kitchen cabinet. Anthony comes back from the bathroom. Where will Anthony look for his medication?

Late one night old Mrs. Peabody is walking home alone. She doesn't like walking home alone in the dark because she is always afraid that someone will jump out at her and rob her. She really is a very nervous person. Suddenly, out of the shadows comes a man. He wants to ask Mrs. Peabody what time it is, so he walks toward her. When Mrs. Peabody sees the man coming toward her, she starts to tremble and says, 'Take my purse, just don't hurt me, please!' Why did Mrs. Peabody say that?

Today James is going to Claire's house for the first time. He is going there for tea, and he is looking forward to seeing Claire's dog, which she talks about all the time. James likes dogs very much. When James arrives at Claire's house, Claire opens the door. Behind her stands a huge dog, almost as big as James! James says, 'Claire, I love your dog!' Is it true what James said?

A burglar who has just robbed a shop is making his way home. As he walks home, a policeman on his beat sees him drop his glove. He doesn't know the man is a burglar; he just wants to tell him he dropped his glove. But when the policeman shouts out to the burglar, 'Hey, you! Stop!' the burglar turns round, sees the policeman and gives himself up. He puts his hands up and admits that he did the break-in at the local shop. Why did the burglar do that when the policeman didn't actually know he had robbed the shop?

Brian is always hungry. Today at school it is his favorite meal: sausages and beans. He is a very greedy boy and he would like to have more sausages than anybody else, even though his mother will have made him a lovely meal at home, too. But everyone is allowed two sausages and no more. When it is Brian's turn to be served, he says, 'Oh, please can I have four sausages, because I won't be having any dinner when I get home!' Why does Brian say this?

Helen waited all year for Christmas, because she knew at Christmas she could ask her parents for a rabbit. Helen wanted a rabbit more than anything in the world. At last Christmas Day arrived, and Helen ran to unwrap the big box her parents had given her. She felt sure it would contain a little rabbit in a cage. But when she opened it, with all the family standing round, she found her present was just a boring old set of encyclopedias, which Helen did not want at all! Still, when Helen's parents asked her how she liked her Christmas present, she said, 'It's lovely, thank you. It's just what I wanted.' Why did Helen say that?

During the war, the Red Army captured a member of the Blue Army. They wanted to know where the Blue Army's tanks were hidden. They knew the tanks were either in the mountains or in the sea. They knew the prisoner would not want to reveal the location, but they also knew he would try to lie. The prisoner is very brave. When the Red Army asks him where the tanks are, he says, 'They are in the mountains.' Why did the prisoner say that, given that the tanks really were in the mountains?

Simon is a big liar. Simon's brother Jim knows this; he knows that Simon never tells the truth! Now yesterday Simon stole Jim's ping-pong paddle, and Jim knows Simon has hidden it somewhere, though he can't find it. He's very cross. So he finds Simon and he says, 'Where is my ping-pong paddle? You must have hidden it either in the cupboard or under your bed, because I've looked everywhere else. Where is it, in the cupboard or under your bed?' Simon tells him the paddle is under his bed. Why will Jim look in the cupboard for the paddle?

One day Aunt Jane came to visit Peter. Now Peter loves his aunt very much, but today she is wearing a new hat; a new hat which Peter thinks is very ugly indeed. Peter thinks his aunt looks silly in it, and much nicer in her old hat. But when Aunt Jane asks Peter, 'How do you like my new hat?', Peter says, 'Oh, it's very nice.' Why does Peter say that?

Late one night, Mr. Brown is on his way to bed when he hears a noise downstairs. He goes down to investigate and finds that his television and stereo have been stolen. He notices a window has been forced open. The next day, when the police come, Mr. Brown says, 'I'm just glad they didn't take the cat too!' Why did Mr. Brown say that?

Sarah and Tom are going on a picnic. It is Tom's idea, he says it is going to be a lovely sunny day for a picnic. But just as they are unpacking the food, it starts to rain, and soon they are both soaked to the skin. Sarah is cross. She says, 'Oh yes, what a lovely day for a picnic alright!' Why does Sarah say that?

Jill wanted to buy a kitten, so she went to see Mrs. Smith who had lots of kittens she didn't want. Mrs. Smith loved the kittens, and she wouldn't do anything to harm them, though she couldn't keep them all herself. When Jill visited she wasn't sure she wanted one of Mrs. Smith's kittens, since they were all males and she had wanted a female. But Mrs. Smith said, 'If no one buys the kittens I'll just have to drown them!' Why did Mrs. Smith say that?

Mike, a nine-year-old boy, often forgets to brush his teeth. One day his Mum says to him, 'Now Mike, do you brush your teeth twice a day?' Mike says, 'Oh yes, of course I do!' In fact he hasn't brushed his teeth for two days. Why did Mike say what he said?
Sarah is bored. She has nothing to do. She picks up a banana and puts it to her ear like a telephone. She says, 'Hello, who's there?' Why does Sarah put the banana to her ear?

Daniel and Jessica's grandfather was very ill in the hospital. He was not expected to live much longer. Yesterday, the family received the sad news that Grandfather had passed away. When Jessica is told the news, she bursts into tears. Daniel says to his mother, 'I'm not going to cry. Grandpa wouldn't want us to.' Why did Daniel say that?

Anna's mother had spent a long time making Anna's favorite meal: fish and chips. But when she brought it in to Anna, she was watching TV, and she didn't even look up, or say thank you. Anna's mother was cross. She said, 'Well, that's very nice, isn't it! That's what I call politeness!' Why did Anna's mother say that?
Two boys, Tom and Sam, are walking past a bakery. Tom says, 'Mm, that bread smells wonderful, I'm so hungry I could eat a horse!' Is it true what Tom said?

Late one night, a man is walking past a cemetery. He hears a tapping sound. Frightened, he stops to investigate, and he finds an old man tapping a chisel on a gravestone. The old man explains, 'They spelled my name wrong on this gravestone.' Why does the old man say his name is spelled wrong on the gravestone?

Emma's class went on a school trip to the zoo. Emma's favorite animal at the zoo was the elephant. When she came home, her brother asked her, 'How big was the elephant?' Emma said, 'Oh, the elephant was as big as a mountain!' Is it true that the elephant was as big as a mountain?

Mark and his sister Lucy are playing tag in the backyard. After a few minutes of chasing, Lucy collapses dramatically on the lawn and lies still with her eyes closed. Mark comes over and pretends to check her pulse with a serious face. Lucy then opens one eye and giggles. Why did Lucy lie down with her eyes closed?

Sam was making a sandwich. He took out the bread, opened the jar of peanut butter, and started spreading it. But he was thinking about his upcoming test, and accidentally he put the peanut butter on the bread in a sandwich shape with the slices in the wrong order. His brother walked in, saw the sandwich, and laughed. Sam asked his brother, 'What are you laughing at?' His brother said, 'You've made a peanut butter sandwich on the outside instead of the inside.' Why did Sam make the sandwich wrong?

A little boy named Kevin has just learned about the planets in school. He runs home and tells his mother, 'Mom! I'm going to walk to Pluto tomorrow!' His mother smiles and says, 'That sounds like a great plan, sweetheart.' Why did Kevin's mother respond that way?

Two old friends, John and Bill, hadn't seen each other in twenty years. They met by chance in a cafe. John said, 'Bill, my old friend! I would have recognized you anywhere; you haven't changed a bit!' In truth, Bill had aged considerably and looked very different. Why did John say that?

Susan is a champion runner. She won her last race in record time. Today she has another race. As she lines up at the starting line, her teammate says, 'Now don't go and lose this one.' What does the teammate mean?

Linda's dog had to go to the vet for an operation. The next day, Linda told her young son, 'Don't worry, the dog is just away on a special vacation, but he'll be fine.' In truth, the dog had died on the operating table. Why did Linda say that?

Henry, a clumsy boy, slipped and fell flat on his face while walking through the cafeteria. The whole cafeteria saw it. As he got up, his friend Greg called out, 'Smooth move, Henry!' What does Greg mean?

A poor man went to a wealthy neighbor asking to borrow money for his sick child's medicine. The wealthy man refused. Later that day, the wealthy man's dog ran away. The poor man, walking by, saw the dog and brought it back to the wealthy man. The wealthy man tried to give him a reward. The poor man said, 'No thank you. I help out of kindness, not for money.' Why did the poor man refuse the reward?

Eight-year-old Maggie wanted a pony for her birthday more than anything in the world. On her birthday, her parents gave her a stuffed pony instead of a real one. Maggie smiled and said, 'Thank you, it's perfect.' Later that night, her mother heard her crying in her room. Why did Maggie smile and say thank you?

A new student joined Mark's class. Mark wanted to make him feel welcome. He went up to the new student at lunch and said, 'There's an empty seat at our table. Come sit with us.' Why did Mark say that?
Two children, Anna and Mia, are playing a game where they pretend to be doctors. Anna takes a wooden block and holds it up to Mia's chest. Anna says, 'Your heart sounds fine.' What is Anna doing?

Two thieves planned to rob a bank. They knew the police were watching them. Thief A says to Thief B in a public place, where they suspect police are listening, 'We'll do the bank job on Tuesday at noon.' In fact, they had planned to do it on Wednesday at midnight. Why did Thief A say that?

Anna was nervous about giving her first big presentation at work. She had practiced for weeks. After she gave the talk, her boss said, 'You really hit it out of the park, Anna!' What does her boss mean?

Tom and Jerry are playing a game. Tom takes a stick and pretends it is a sword. He waves it around and says, 'I am a brave knight!' Jerry runs and grabs a pot to put on his head. He says, 'And I am a knight too!' What are Tom and Jerry doing?

Lisa knew her sister Carol was secretly afraid of spiders. One April Fools' Day, Lisa put a rubber spider in Carol's bed. When Carol pulled back the covers, she screamed and jumped. Lisa burst out laughing. Carol said, 'Lisa, that wasn't funny!' What was Lisa trying to do?

Marie left her car at the auto shop because the engine was making noise. The mechanic told her it would cost $200. When she came back, the bill was $400. The mechanic explained he found additional problems. Marie suspected he was overcharging her. She said calmly, 'Oh wonderful, what a great surprise.' What does Marie mean?

Ben's grandfather had been very sick for months. When Ben visited him in the hospital, his grandfather smiled weakly and said, 'I'm doing great. Don't worry about me.' Ben looked at the tubes and machines around him and saw the tired look in his grandfather's eyes. Was the grandfather telling Ben the truth?

Tony saw his friend Carl at the grocery store. Carl was sneaking a chocolate bar into his pocket without paying. Tony pretended he hadn't seen and walked the other way. Later, Tony confronted Carl privately and said, 'I saw what you did.' Carl looked embarrassed and said, 'I didn't want to lose your friendship.' Why did Tony confront Carl privately rather than at the store?

Five-year-old Lila was upset because her parents wouldn't let her have ice cream before dinner. She stomped to her room and slammed the door. A minute later she yelled, 'I'm not coming out ever again!' Did Lila really mean she would never come out?

Ethan was applying for a competitive scholarship. He had to write an essay. When he finished, his friend Rachel read it. She thought it was full of grammar mistakes and weak arguments. But she said, 'It's really thoughtful. I'm sure the committee will appreciate it.' Why did Rachel say that?

A magician at a children's party pulled a rabbit out of a hat. The young children gasped and clapped. A nine-year-old boy named Sam called out, 'I know how you did it! The rabbit was hidden in a secret compartment!' The magician smiled and continued without confirming. Why did the magician not confirm Sam's explanation?

You believe the dog ate your homework. Your sister believes the cat ate it. In fact, you accidentally left the homework at school. What does your sister believe happened to the homework?

After a piano recital, the music teacher came to congratulate the students. She approached young Andrew and said in front of his parents, 'You played quite well, considering you don't really have much musical talent.'

You believe your mother is at home today. Your sister Anna believes she went to the grocery store. In fact, your mother is at the doctor's office. Where does Anna believe your mother is?

Olivia and her grandmother were having tea. Olivia was telling her grandmother about her new boyfriend. Olivia said, 'He's wonderful, you'll really like him.' Her grandmother said, 'I hope so. The last one you brought home was awful.'

Cara handed her grandmother a birthday card. Her grandmother opened it, read it, and said, 'Thank you, dear, this is lovely.'

James went out for dinner with his colleague Anna. They both ordered the same pasta dish. After the meal, the waiter brought the bill. James said, 'Thank you for joining me tonight, I enjoyed our conversation.' Anna smiled and said, 'Me too, it was lovely.'
